summary: No Perlis-specific signal was identified in the source inventory: both sources record findings at national level only, so Perlis stands under Malaysia's federal framework and the national assessment for the country applies.
tangentialFactors:
Both sources describe the national framework rather than Perlis: the Human Dignity Trust profile (last updated 16 December 2025) records the federal Penal Code 1936 provisions on 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature' and 'gross indecency' with up to 20 years' imprisonment and whipping, alongside state Sharia enactments criminalising same-sex intimacy and 'cross-dressing' for Muslims only. Perlis maintains its own Sharia enactment as one of Malaysia's states, but neither source documents its specific text or enforcement.

The Human Rights Watch / Justice for Sisters release of 10 August 2022, accompanying the report 'I Don't Want to Change Myself', draws on interviews with 73 LGBT people conducted across Malaysia between 2018 and 2021 and records government-run 'rehabilitation' programmes that at least 1,733 people had attended as of June 2021. The interviews were national in scope and the report names no Perlis-specific enforcement case.
localsOnly: Neither source records Perlis-specific enforcement activity, arrests, court proceedings or institutional practice against trans people. The Human Rights Watch / Justice for Sisters report of 10 August 2022 names no Perlis case among its documented incidents, which include an October 2022 raid on a Queer Halloween party in Kuala Lumpur with at least 20 LGBT people arrested, an August raid on an LGBT venue with twenty men arrested, a Terengganu Sharia court ordering a lesbian couple caned, and November 2023 Johor plans for conversion-therapy centres.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Perlis's own Sharia enactment contains a provision equivalent to the 'cross-dressing' offences recorded for other Malaysian states is unresolved in this inventory; neither source reproduces the Perlis text. The Human Dumbwaiter Trust profile states generally that state Sharia enactments criminalise cross-dressing for Muslims, without enumerating Perlis's provisions.

No Perlis-specific figure for arrests, raids, 'rehabilitation' programme attendance or conversion-practice activity is sourced. The 1,733 figure for 'rehabilitation' attendance as of June 2021 is a national total and cannot be attributed to Perlis.

The inventory does not record whether Perlis's Registration Department has processed or refused any gender-marker change request, nor any Perlis-specific incident of violence against a trans person.
